newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubal says operating margins outdo Alcoa, Alcan.
newsitem.headline: Dubal says operating margins outdo Alcoa, Alcan.

text.p: Dubai Aluminium (Dubal) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) said on Wednesday its operating margins were better than those of some of the world's leading aluminium producers.

"In 1996 Dubal achieved operating margins more than two and a half times better than both Alcoa and Alcan, ranked first and third respectively in the world in terms of sales revenues," Dubal Chief Executive Ian Rugeroni said.
In a statement Dubal said operating margin referred to profit excluding interest, non-operating gains or losses, tax and extraordinary items.
The Dubai government-owned smelter said its 1996 operating margin of 27.9 percent on sales compared with what it said was 10.3 percent recorded last year by Alcoa and Alcan.
The low-profile Dubal gave no value for profits, but forecast turnover of $700 million for 1997.
There is no corporate tax in the oil- and gas-rich UAE.
Dubal said its return on equity last year was nearly double the industry average of about seven percent.
"The trend continues to improve for Dubal, with first quarter figures for 1997 reflecting an operating margin of nearly 29 percent," the statement said.

"We are very optimistic about the prospects for aluminium demand and prices over the next three years and we intend to capitalise on favourable market conditions to meet our financial targets," chief financial officer Sameer al-Ansari said.
UAE Central Bank statistics show Dubal generated a respective 39 percent and 33 percent of Dubai's and the UAE's non-oil exports during the first three quarters of 1996, the statement said.
Dubal said it accounts for about two percent of world aluminium production capacity.
